stories.headline: Poilievre's US trip culminates in Joe Rogan podcast appearance to make case against tariffs
stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre spent a week in the US meeting officials and appearing on The Joe Rogan Experience podcast, using the platform to argue against US tariffs and promote his auto sector plan. The trip included meetings with Texas Governor Abbott and Michigan auto leaders.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada holds interest rate at 2.25% amid Iran war inflation concerns
stories.summary: The Bank of Canada kept its key interest rate unchanged at 2.25% for the third consecutive meeting, citing economic weakness but growing concerns about oil price inflation from the Middle East conflict. Governor Macklem warned the bank would act if energy price increases become persistent.

stories.headline: Carney's international travel approach draws analysis as PM logs record time abroad
stories.summary: Analysis reveals PM Mark Carney spent 84 days traveling internationally in his first year, significantly more than predecessors Trudeau (63 days) and Harper (34 days). Recent trips included Nordic summit in Oslo and meetings with UK PM Starmer on Middle East crisis.

stories.headline: NDP MP Lori Idlout crosses floor to Liberals as party leadership race continues
stories.summary: Nunavut NDP MP Lori Idlout defected to the Liberal caucus, citing ability to better serve constituents. The move brings Liberals to 170 seats as the NDP leadership race continues with five candidates including frontrunner Avi Lewis.

stories.headline: Canada maintains non-combat role as pressure mounts over Middle East involvement
stories.summary: Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed Canadian Armed Forces are 'not involved in the prosecution' of the Iran war, despite having members in the region. This comes amid US pressure on NATO allies to help secure the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Canada knew 'from the beginning' CAF wouldn't help attack Iran: minister

stories.headline: Former Bloc Québécois MP arrested on sexual assault charges involving minors
stories.summary: Pascal-Pierre Paillé, who represented Louis-Hébert from 2008-2011, was arrested by Quebec City police on charges including sexual assault and sexual contact with minors. The alleged incidents span from 2006 to August 2024.

stories.headline: Analysis shows Carney's first budget outspends Trudeau plans by $67.6 billion
stories.summary: A Fraser Institute analysis found PM Carney's 2025 budget will spend $67.6 billion more over four years than Trudeau's projected spending, with combined deficits reaching $321.7 billion from 2025-2030. The analysis sparked debate over fiscal priorities and spending discipline.

articles.title: PM Carney's first budget outspends Trudeau's plan by $67.6 billion over next four years

stories.headline: Defence Investment Agency awards $307 million rifle replacement contract to Colt Canada
stories.summary: The government awarded Colt Canada a contract to manufacture over 65,000 rifles to replace aging C7 and C8 rifles that have been in service for 35 years. Phase 1 involves production of 30,000 rifles valued at $307 million as part of modernizing Canadian Armed Forces equipment.

articles.title: Defence Investment Agency awards contract to replace current Canadian Armed Forces assault rifles

stories.headline: Terrebonne by-election set for April 13 as Bloc and Liberals face rematch
stories.summary: The Supreme Court-ordered re-run of the Terrebonne election will take place April 13, featuring the same candidates: Liberal Tatiana Auguste versus Bloc Québécois candidate Nathalie Sinclair-Desgagné. The seat is crucial as Liberals seek to secure their parliamentary majority.
